summary: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Cutting Administrative Requirements for Excellence in Patient Care (CARE) (CMS-3484-P) Overview On Nov. 5, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) issued the Cutting Administrative Requirements for Excellence in Patient Care (CARE) proposed rule. This rule proposes regulatory revisions to the Conditions of Participation (CoPs), Conditions for Coverage (CfCs), and Requirements for Participation for Medicare- and Medicaid-participating providers and suppliers (collectively referred to as CoPs). These revisions would reduce costs, increase transparency, enhance flexibility for providers to deliver innovative patient care, and streamline existing regulations. It also proposes to rescind certain Medicaid institutional payment transparency reporting requirements to reduce burden for states and institutional providers. Background CMS conducted a comprehensive review of the CoPs for all 21 provider and supplier types, as well as some payment policies, to identify opportunities to reduce administrative burden while maintaining patient safety and quality care. The agency identified obsolete, outdated, and excessively burdensome regulations that CMS proposes to eliminate or reform to enhance the effectiveness of facility operations and reduce unnecessary burden or other costs, with a particular focus on freeing up resources that healthcare providers could otherwise use to improve patient health and safety. Collectively, CMS estimates the proposals would save $320 million, returning more than 3.26 million hours of staff time to providers. This proposed rule would alleviate unnecessary regulatory burden through deregulation in the following ways: Hospitals Remove the staff training requirements for transfer protocols and emergency services readiness (both currently effective), and obstetric (OB) care (otherwise effective Jan. 1, 2027). Remove the OB care-specific Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) requirements (otherwise effective Jan. 1, 2027). Propose to establish new requirements regarding patients’ rights related to birth tissue collection by hospitals that provide OB care services, including standards for informed consent and policies and procedures to support families requesting their birth tissues for cultural, religious, or personal reasons. Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) Remove the staff training requirements related to emergency services readiness (currently effective) and OB care (otherwise effective Jan. 1, 2027). Remove the OB care-specific Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) requirements (otherwise effective Jan. 1, 2027). Propose to establish new requirements regarding patients’ rights related to birth tissue collection by CAHs that provide OB care services, including standards for informed consent and policies and procedures to support families requesting their birth tissues for cultural, religious, or personal reasons. Revise regulations to clarify current CMS policy that CAH distance eligibility determinations are based on proximity to hospitals that provide acute care inpatient services or another CAH. Implement new statutory requirements to allow CAHs that meet certain qualifying criteria, as defined by the statute, to be exempt from the distance eligibility requirements. Long-Term Care (LTC) Facilities Remove the COVID-19 vaccine requirements related to educating staff about the benefits and risks, offering the vaccine, and documenting these actions. Streamline the remaining COVID-19 vaccine requirements for residents. Remove the continuing respiratory illness data reporting requirement while retaining the requirement for specific reporting during a future Secretary-declared public health emergency (PHE). Modify the requirement for LTC facilities to provide a state ombudsman with notice of resident transfers related to emergent care. Revise the requirements for the active involvement of representatives of direct care staff in conducting the LTC facility assessment. Revise the physical environment requirements to exempt existing facilities from the room occupancy and bathroom facility standards. Intermediate Care Facilities for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICFs/IID) Remove the requirements related to educating staff about the COVID-19 vaccine and its benefits and risks, offering it to them, and documenting these actions. Streamline the remaining COVID-19 vaccine requirements for clients. Rural Emergency Hospitals (REHs) Remove expired COVID-19 and seasonal influenza reporting requirements related to ongoing data reporting and staff vaccination. Remove REH data reporting requirements during a PHE. Physical Environment Life Safety Code (LSC) and Health Care Facilities Code (HCFC) Updates and Emergency and Standby Powers Systems (ESPS) Codes Adopt the 2024 editions of National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) LSC and HCFC and the 2022 edition of the ESPS Codes. Outside Window or Door Requirement Remove the requirement that patient care areas have access to natural light and ventilation through exterior windows and doors for hospitals, CAHs, and other providers with similar regulations (Religious Nonmedical Health Care Institutions, LTC facilities, ICFs/IID and hospice inpatient care facilities). Waiver Authority Codify in the regulations CMS’ authority to permit facilities to comply with specific provisions of a newer edition of the LSC or HCFC. Medicaid Payment Transparency for Nursing Facilities and ICFs/IID Rescind the following Medicaid institutional payment transparency reporting requirements to reduce burden for states and institutional providers: The percentage of Medicaid payments for nursing facility services spent on compensation for direct care workers, The percentage of Medicaid payments for nursing facility services spent on compensation for support staff, and The percentage of Medicaid payments for ICFs/IID services spent on compensation for support staff. Comment Solicitations CMS is including comment solicitations in this proposed rule to obtain input from interested parties related to the following topics: Allowing LTC facility residents to opt-out of having a discharge notice sent to the state ombudsman office; Strategies to minimize burden for hospitals and CAHs to comply with ongoing respiratory illness and PHE infectious illness data reporting requirements; Approaches to allow flexibility for providers regarding the requirement for physician supervision of certified registered nurse anesthetists (CRNAs); Expanding the scope of practice of physician assistants and nurse practitioners providing care in LTC facilities, especially as it pertains to performing visits currently required by a physician; Revising criteria for transplant program initial certification to reduce barriers to entry for new transplant programs while maintaining patient safety and ensuring the transplant program’s competence; and Future policies to address Medicaid institutional workforce shortages and strengthen the institutional workforce. View the final rule on the Federal Register at: https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/2026-22812/medicare-and-medicaid-programs-cutting-administrative-requirements-for-excellence-in-patient-care .
